hatch: Disable HW_RAMP until bq25710 ICO mode is changed The charge hw ramp implementation in the bq25710 is implemented by enabling ICO (input current optimizer) mode, waiting for it to complete, then reading optimized current value from the IIN_DPM register. This is not the correct use case for ICO mode. It has certain issues, the most serious of which is that if a battery isn't present or if the battery doesn't have enough charge to power the system, it will cause PPVAR_VSYS to collapse. To avoid the issue mentioned above, disable the hw ramp config until the hw ramp implementation of the bq25710 is reworked. BUG=b:126229130 BRANCH=none TEST=make BOARD=hatch and verifed that ICO mode is not longer activated. Change-Id: I736c21ad269742650cc62939995c4caa77154b6b Signed-off-by: Scott Collyer <scollyer@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1512135 Commit-Ready: Scott Collyer <scollyer@chromium.org> Tested-by: Scott Collyer <scollyer@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org>

debugd: Return true when doing redudant coredump setting There's been crashes in debugd in GetDBusError, and the only reason those seem possible is by the ErrorPtr being null. I looked through all the DBus method implementations in debugd, and this was the only case I found where a method returns false but does not set the ErrorPtr to an object. Rather than having these return an error (since this case is just a redundant call, which we log) just have them return true which should fix any crashes as a result of these calls. CHROMIUM: config: Modify rcu stall timeout to match default (60 => 21) Back in 2012 in commit c896054f75f9 ("rcu: Reduce default RCU CPU stall warning timeout"), the default stall timeout changed from 60 seconds to 21 seconds. Presumably we never explicitly picked our old value of 60 seconds but just took the old default. However, as an artifact of the split config system we didn't automatically get an update when the default changed. Let's update things. NOTE: I don't expect this to immediately help anything, I just noticed it while trying to debug chromium:916228 and it seemed like a good idea to fix. BUG=chromium:916228 TEST=modprobe configs; zgrep RCU_CPU_STALL_TIMEOUT /proc/config.gz Change-Id: Ie5b307f4c0c4e27b1490cefa6f91fb48725aa56e Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1503677 Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org>

driver: lis2dh: Add support for lng2dm Looking at 4.19 kernel (drivers/iio/accel/st_accel_core.c), LNG2DM has the same interface as LIS2DH but a resolution of 8 bits only. In consequence, basic handling of LIS2DE and LNG2DM should be identical. FIFO and interrupt are not supported.
